STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: The If-None-Match matcher holds up: 20,000 randomized comparisons against `http.ServeContent` produced zero mismatches, and the HEAD and 304 wire behaviour is correct. Three correctness problems reproduced: Flush sends bytes early (which the approved-difference line forbids), a handler's ETag can be duplicated or replaced, and a 103 after an explicit 200 reaches the client where net/http drops it. All probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start.
FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probes `middleware/zz_probe*_etag_test.go` were created and removed)
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Approved difference "Flush must not send bytes before the response completes" does not hold. `ETag(...)` with `w.Write("a")`, `Flush()` gave `rec.Body == "a"` before the handler returned (`P1 REPRODUCED`). The code and `TestETagFlushStopsBuffering` both do this, as criterion 7 asks, so the approved-difference line contradicts the spec. The orchestrator must decide which one is intended.
- [blocking] Criterion 3 (handler ETag never altered) fails. `finish()` tests `h.Get("ETag") == ""`, so:
  - A handler that sets `w.Header()["ETag"] = []string{""}` gets the body hash in its place (`P4 REPRODUCED`).
  - A handler that sets the non-canonical key `w.Header()["etag"] = {"\"v1\""}` ends up with two lines on the wire: `Etag: "<sha256>"` and `etag: "v1"` (`P5 REPRODUCED`).
- [blocking] Wrapper differs from net/http, and the difference is not on the approved list. `WriteHeader(200); WriteHeader(103); Write("x")` gives the recorder code 200 unwrapped but 103 wrapped (`P3`). net/http ignores a 1xx after a final status. Criterion 6 says 1xx is "forwarded immediately", so the spec and the differential rule disagree; decide which applies.
- [minor] `WriteHeader(101)` gives the same wire bytes as unwrapped, but the wrapper triggers `http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call ... startStreaming` in the server log (`P11`). Not a client-visible difference.
- [minor] The ETag covers only the body, so two responses with the same bytes but different Content-Type share a tag. A JSON request carrying the text/html tag gets a 304 with no Content-Type (`P9`, reproduced). The spec defines this, but the doc comment doesn't mention it.
- [minor] `Last-Modified` is removed on 304, which the criteria don't list. It matches net/http's `writeNotModified` only when an ETag is present.
CHECKS:
- P6, 20,000 random If-None-Match inputs vs `http.ServeContent` with the same ETag (quotes, W/, /, commas, tabs, a/x/X, 0x7F, 0xFF, tag splices, handler ETag variants) -> pass, 0 mismatches.
- P7, nested `ETag(ETag(h))`: plain 200 with body, matching If-None-Match -> 304 -> pass.
- P8, real `httptest.NewServer`: HEAD -> 200, ETag is the sha256 of the body, Content-Length 5 -> pass. GET with `W/` request -> 304, no Content-Type or Content-Length, empty body -> pass.
- P12, `http.NewResponseController(w).SetWriteDeadline` through Unwrap on a real server -> pass (nil error).
- P13, HEAD with Flush -> committed, no ETag, no 304 -> pass.
- Handler-set Last-Modified, Vary, Cache-Control, Expires and Content-Location are kept on 304 -> pass (existing test).
- Other methods pass the original writer through (existing test) -> pass.
- Sibling check: Hijack/Push error wording matches compress.go; Unwrap exists; README row and link are alphabetical and the row width matches -> pass.
- TRIGGERED CHECKS: invariants (20k seeded loop) pass; wrapper differential fails (P1, P3); nesting passes; HTTP responses pass (P8, P13). The -race concurrent test was not re-run by me.
OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Which Flush behaviour is intended: criterion 7 (flush writes buffered bytes) or the approved-difference line (no bytes before completion)?
- Should a 1xx after an explicit 200 be forwarded (criterion 6 wording) or dropped like net/http?
